verdict.rationale: OpenTofu offers `tofu plan` speculative plans that preview changes without applying them, and `tofu test`, which creates temporary real infrastructure, checks assertions, then destroys what it created. Multi-environment provider configs (dev/staging/prod) and the `-exclude` flag help keep tests away from production, but isolation depends on the user wiring up separate accounts or credentials; there is no built-in sandbox. Missing for 10: a first-party sandbox or mock environment, documented guarantees that tests are isolated from production, and independent or hands-on corroboration of safe testing workflows.
